target_customer: Collectors and players of Magic the Gathering cards buying and selling singles
problem: Buying and selling collectible cards online risks counterfeits and slow, uncertain price discovery. Mage ran a live bid and ask marketplace where the company verified every card.
business_model: Marketplace take rate with company run verification and fulfillment

founders.name: Peer Richelsen
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as later co-founder and chairman of Cal.com.

founders.name: Malte Delfs
founders.background_notes: Named CTO in the shutdown coverage.

exit.reason: The CEO said COVID-19 cut revenue by 60 percent and the company had not found a quick route to profitability; remaining cash went to extended severance.

technical_complexity.rationale: A bid and ask matching marketplace plus inventory verification is standard web engineering; the hard part was physical logistics and warehouses.

defensibility.rationale: Established marketplaces already had the buyers and sellers, and verification and logistics were operational costs, not a moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large MTG marketplaces kept their position; no source shows them copying Mage. Mage shut down in March 2020.

market_need_then: Counterfeit and condition concerns in collectible cards plus an active Magic secondary market motivated verified trading, but no demand metrics were published.

branding.name_origin: Mage is a Magic the Gathering term; the company began as Snapcardster in 2016 and became Mage during YC W19. Reason for the choice is not stated.

identity.voice_and_tone: Playful pitch language such as transactions happen automagically

branding.brand_signature: The word automagically for bid and ask matches

rebrands.why: Rebranded during the YC W19 batch per shutdown coverage; reason not stated

branding.community_and_virality: Covered on Product Hunt in November 2019 and by Magic community press, and its Klarna financing option drew controversy in early 2020.

brand_strength.rationale: Fits the Magic theme and was memorable to players, but shared its name with many unrelated companies and had limited reach.

pivots.to: Mage bid and ask marketplace with verification and warehouses
pivots.why: Relaunched in summer 2019 with bid and ask features and planned North American and European warehouses

outcome_analysis: Mage began as Snapcardster in 2016, rebranded in YC W19 and relaunched as a bid and ask marketplace with company verification. Its North American warehouse stalled on visa issues in early 2020, then COVID-19 cut revenue by 60 percent and the founders shut down in March 2020 because profitability was not near.
notes: Seed investors (Y Combinator and Twitch angels) come from one outlet, Hipsters of the Coast; the amount is not stated and the date 2019-01 is the YC W19 batch start, approximate. A June 2019 article said a second round was planned by end of 2019; no evidence it closed. Competitor list empty because the June 2019 launch article names no rivals and the only competitor search returned current-day data. Mage the AI company results are unrelated. Founder education and prior employers not found. Two outlets (Epicstream and Hipsters of the Coast) cover the shutdown.
